articleTitle: Improving Brain Tumor Detection Efficiency with Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: An aberrant cell growth in the brain is called a brain tumor. These growths may be malignant (cancerous) or benign (non-cancerous). Benign tumors are generally slower-growing and less likely to invade nearby tissues, while malignant tumors can grow more rapidly and may spread to other parts of the brain or the body. Delay in the detection of a brain tumor may result in the tumor growing larger and potentially becoming more challenging to treat. Hence, early detection and treatment of a brain tumor are crucial for treatment options, preventing further damage, improved prognosis, and for preventing complications. This paper aims to improve the performance of brain tumor detection using Convolution Neural Network (CNN) with accuracy 98%. Transfer Learning technique is applied on CNN after taking a pre-trained model on a large dataset and fine-tuning it.

articleTitle: Intelligent Connected Vehicle Intrusion Detection and Mitigation: An Analysis of Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: IoT and AI created a Transportation Management System, resulting in the Internet of Vehicles. Intelligent vehicles are combined with contemporary communication technologies (5G) to achieve automated driving and adequate mobility. IoV faces security issues in the next five (5) areas: data safety, V2X communication safety, platform safety, Intermediate Commercial Vehicles (ICV) safety, and intelligent device safety. Numerous types of AI models have been created to reduce the outcome infiltration risks on ICVs. The need to integrate confidence, transparency, and repeatability into the creation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for the safety of ICV and to deliver harmless transport systems, on the other hand, has led to an increase in explainable AI (XAI). Therefore, the space of this analysis protected the XAI models employed in ICV intrusion detection systems (IDSs), their taxonomies, and available research concerns. The study's findings demonstrate that, despite its relatively recent submission to ICV, XAI is a potential explore area for those looking to increase the net effect of ICVs. The paper also demonstrates that XAI's greater transparency will help it gain acceptance in the vehicle industry.

articleTitle: Enhancing Neurofuzzy Plasticity: A Fusion of LSTM and Artificial Neurogenesis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to address the dead neuron and stability-plasticity dilemma in deep neuro-fuzzy systems. The proposed solution is a neuro-fuzzy network with Long-short term memory (LSTM) based Artificial Neurogenesis (ANG), which combines the strengths of both deep neural networks and fuzzy logic. This hybridized model offers several benefits, including improved adaptability, scalability, and interpretability. By leveraging LSTM memory cells, the framework enables dynamic adaptation of the network. The proposed model, evaluated under given parameters, demonstrated significant improvements in accuracy compared to existing methods. Extensive testing further verified the hypothesis, with results reflected in accuracy graphs and various other performance metrics

articleTitle: Fabric Defect Detection Systems and Methods in India: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: India's textile industry heavily relies on efficient fabric defect detection for maintaining product quality and production efficiency. This review paper comprehensively analyzes fabric defect detection systems and methods, encompassing both traditional and recent advancements. We explore the limitations of manual inspection and discuss how traditional techniques based on statistical and texture analysis provided improvements but lacked adaptability to complex defect patterns. The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning with convolutional neural networks (CNNs), has revolutionized the field by offering high accuracy, the ability to learn intricate patterns directly from fabric images, and the potential for automation. The review further delves into how other AI techniques like Generative Adversarial networks(GANs),autoencoders, and transfer learning can further enhance AI-based fabric defect detection. We conclude by highlighting the ongoing challenges, including the need for extensive, well-labeled datasets and the importance of improving model interpretability. By fostering continued research in AI for fabric defect detection, India's textile industry can achieve significant advancements in ensuring superior product quality and streamlined production.

articleTitle: Exploring Network Security Metric and Enhancing the Secure Computing for Cloud through Honeypot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Rapid user growth is causing problems with website performance, web hosting, and data space and memory allocation, all of which can directly or indirectly result in data loss. We use cloud computing techniques to provide services that are dependable, quick, and affordable. This technology is developing at a rapid rate, which increases the possibility that hostile people will breach its security. Using honeypots is one method of rerouting harmful traffic away from computers. It's a massive method that has improved system security somewhat. The idea of Honeypot is applied to a file-sharing program that is hosted on a cloud server, taking into consideration the several legal concerns that could arise from installing Honeypot on servers owned by third-party cloud vendors. This research presents a novel method to identify attacks in cloud-based environments by discussing the use of honeypots for security and detecting assaults in such environments.

articleTitle: Advancing Beach Litter Detection with Split and Federated Learning Collaborative Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The rising threat of environmental pollution in an era of rapid urbanization and industrialization necessitates a novel approach to environmental monitoring and management. The growing rise of pollutants, environmental concerns, empha-sises the escalating necessity for prompt and efficient measures to address this problem. While conventional methods struggle with the limitation of real-time monitoring and adaptability to a multitude of environmental conditions, emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and machine learning provide holistic solutions to address these problems. The existing machine learning-based approaches have limited adaptability to varied environmental settings, privacy concerns due to centralized processing and scalability issues for covering a large geographical area. Addressing these constraints, this paper proposes a distributed model that uses a combined Split and Federated Learning approach for identifying environmental contaminants within images taken at various beaches. By decentralizing model training, the proposed model ensures privacy by allowing collaboration between different data collection devices at various locations without the exchange of raw data. The proposed model achieves Dice Score Coefficient(DSC) of 88.6% and Intersection over Union (IoU) score of 68% and hence emerges as a more resilient and privacy-protecting solution that offers an adaptable solution to beach litter image segmentation for efficient environmental monitoring,

articleTitle: AutoCoach: An Automated Playing Eleven Selection Framework in Cricket
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Cricket is one of the famous international sports where both teams select their best eleven against each other from the available pool of players usually a total size of 15 to 16. The team selection process is usually performed by the coaches using their observation and consultations etc. In simple words, by looking at the possible combinations of opposite sides, the best possible combinations are suggested. In our work, we tried to automate this process using machine learning models like Support Vector Regressor, Linear Regression Random Forest regressor etc. To train and test the model, the data was crawled from the Indian Premier League (IPL), which follows 20 over format and data for more than 10 seasons is used. More importantly, multiple related features for batters and bowlers were accumulated to develop all possible combinations for each playing team in a single match. In total, we selected 4 different teams and developed three combinations for each. Then, in a single match between two teams, the combinations were compared based upon accumulative score e.g., matching scores for different combinations are compared with ground truth. In our opinion, this is one of the unique contributions made for automated team selection in cricket specific to the format and encompassing performance indicators not only accumulated from IPL but also from the International Cricket Council (ICC).

articleTitle: Exploration of Inaccessible Fibrins in SEM of RBC using Fractal based Modified Segregation Scoring Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) can be very serious because blood clots in veins can break loose, travel through our bloodstream and lodge in our lungs, blocking blood flow. Aim of this paper is to analyse the depth of blood coagulation and fibrin structure in veins using the proposed MF-DAS method. Using SEM for RBC blood coagulated specimens as the base image, both DVT -patients and normal people images were taken, and the MF-DAS images were obtained, exploring deeper fibrins unexplored by the original SEM images nor by their segmented counterparts, which clearly delineated the fibrins from the rest. The Box counting algorithm is used to find the slope of the SEM images. If the slope value is closer to dimension 2 are called as unaffected images. Or else, if there is more deviation, then the images are blood clot images. The proposed algorithm is used for finding the deep analysis of thrombosis images.

articleTitle: Motion Parameter Estimation of Low Flying UAV Using Acoustic Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Acoustics is developing as a substantial complementary modality to be explored and subjugated in the growth of intelligence and surveillance systems that conventionally rely on technology entrenched in electromagnetic field singularities. Acoustic sensors are desirable due to their passive nature, low cost, durability, and compactness. Also, the propagation of sound energy is not limited to the line of sight. An application of the present scenario is the detection and localization of the sound sources using acoustic sensors on the ground and on-board unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The target's immediate frequency was picked up by an acoustic sensor that was set up on the ground. To estimate flight parameters, an acoustic sensor placed above the ground produces Doppler-shifted frequency time histories. A straight-line trajectory and constant velocity cause the instantaneous frequency received to vary due to the acoustic doppler effect. Based on the instantaneous frequency model, a Nelder-Mead algorithm is used to estimate the motion parameters of the low flying UAV.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Algorithms for Intrusion Detection in IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The increase in the use of the Internet of Things (IoT) to achieve concepts like smart cities and health monitoring brings together a diversity of devices and data flow, which creates an abyss of a diverse range of attacks, which makes it necessary to put in place proper anomaly identification and mitigation mechanisms. Traditional intrusion detection systems cannot cope with versatile attacks, which urges using advanced techniques encompassing concepts like machine learning and deep learning to create a robust and versatile mechanism to identify and mitigate unintended traffic. In this paper, we analyze the efficiency of different deep learning techniques like CNN, LSTM, and XGBoost and compare their efficiency. The paper uses a dual CNN approach, an LSTM with three stacked layers, and XGBoost techniques with cross-validation to reduce overfitting on the IOTBOTNET 2020 dataset. The results show LSTM and XGBoost perform better, achieving an f1 score of 99.97% and 94%, respectively, compared to DUAL CNN, which achieved a score of 62.49 %.

articleTitle: Neuroimaging-Based Age Prediction with Genetic Algorithm for Feature Optimisation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: To build an age prediction model using structural brain MRI data. Finding better ways to use evolutionary algorithm for feature optimisation in age prediction models built from neuroimaging datasets is the main goal of this study. For this procedure to work, structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which record minute information about the brain's anatomy, are used as input data. The use of genetic algorithm is employed to improve the feature extraction procedure. That way, we can choose out traits that are discriminative and helpful, which is a huge boon to age prediction. As the evolutionary algorithm iteratively refines the feature subset, the model's performance and processing efficiency are both enhanced. The next step is to make use of the selected attributes while building a regression or other deep learning model to accurately predict chronological age. In addition to assisting with feature selection, the genetic algorithm also refines the predictive model's hyperparameters, making sure the model is set up optimally for age prediction. Researchers hope that this work will lead to an improved neuroimaging-based age prediction model that outperforms current methods in terms of accuracy and interpretability. An improved understanding of the structural changes in the brain that occur with age is expected to result from using genetic algorithm for feature optimisation, which is thought to reveal important neuroanatomical patterns related to ageing.

articleTitle: Wireless Sensor Network-Driven IoT Solution for Advanced Borewell Rescue Robotics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The fact that deaths from bore wells persist in India is highly alarming, particularly when young people are involved. Since 2009, there have been more than 40 documented child deaths, and the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) reported a worrisome 70% failure rate for rescue efforts. The solution must be found quickly and effectively. In response to this humanitarian problem, this paper has proposed a novel design for a robotics device. This proposed system is a creative illustration of how human interaction and technology may be used in tandem to swiftly evaluate the victims and guarantee their safe release. The main element of this solution is a skillfully designed robotic arm that smoothly integrates Internet of Things (IoT) devices (Rasp Pi or Arduino) and is powered by high-precision servo motors. Among the many features it offers are an advanced APR (Auto Playback Recorder) system, an infrared-based CCTV camera, a strong LED lighting system, advanced sensors (Passive Infrared, Ultrasonic Distance Measurement, Heartbeat, Temperature, and Gas), and a dual-functional mask. Artificial intelligence (AI) is another tactic that will be used in the rescue operation. This paper discusses the pressing need for safe, efficient bore well rescues and offers a comprehensive analysis of the methodology. This project uses cutting edge technology and human collaboration to stop more catastrophes and increase the speed and effectiveness of life-saving procedures in emergency situations. In an effort to contribute to the creation of a more secure and safe future, this research is presented as a critical first step in lowering the death toll related to Indian bore wells.

articleTitle: Efficient Illumination: Arduino-Based Street Light Automation for Energy Savings
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: This research introduces an innovative Arduino-based solution to address energy wastage in street lighting, which activates lights autonomously in the presence of vehicles or pedestrians. The system, leveraging PIR sensors for vehicle detection and LDRs for day-night differentiation, dynamically adjusts LED brightness, ensuring optimal energy utilization. This dual-sensor approach extends the lifespan of street lamps and contributes to a more environmentally friendly urban landscape. The primary objective is to trigger and promote selective street lights, thereby promoting significant energy savings and cost reductions and a sustainable lighting infrastructure tailored to diverse community needs. This research addresses the imperative of resource conservation amid unprecedented population growth and escalating energy demand, offering a pioneering solution for metropolitan areas.

articleTitle: Prediction Model for Suicidal Behavior Disorder Risk Analysis by Correlating Cyber and Real World Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: In the era of internet of things (IoT), people are attentive to express their non verbal behavior on cyber world such as social media by using smart phone, laptop or tablet. People are more active in sharing their daily activities status such as current activity the person is into and personal life situations such as achievement, problem, stress and even any hazardous desire (i.e. suicide). In contrast with real world such as smart home environment, people generally spent their non verbal behavior in term of Activity Daily Livings (ADLs) in associating with smart home sensors. Based on non verbal and verbal behaviors, data are generated from both Cyber and Real world, which are big in volume and variety. However, there is lack of investigating Cyber and Real world data especially in analyzing the risk of committing suicide, considering suicide is a big issues and threats in the society. Therefore, it motivate us to propose prediction model to determine high and low risk of committing suicide by combining two separate approaches such as Activity Recognition (AR) for real world and Sentiment Analysis (SA) for cyber world.

articleTitle: Quaternion Neural Networks as a Polarization-Aware Adaptive Signal-Processing Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: This keynote focuses on quaternion neural networks (QNNs) dealing with polarization information of electromagnetic waves. We give an overview of this field and look into its future.

articleTitle: Wavelet-ANN Based Detection of Fault Location of 2-Bus Connected Power Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The complexity of the power system increases as hundreds of lines due to the penetration of conventional and non-conventional energy sources. Transmitting the power for hundreds of kilometres through large number of transmission lines makes complexity in the network to locate the fault. Thus it is necessary to develop suitable algorithms to identify the location of the fault accurately in presence of large number of transmission lines. In this paper a novel Wavelet-ANN (Artificial Neural Network) based method is developed where the Detailed coefficients (D1 coefficients) obtained from post current signals are used for wavelet analysis. The D1 coefficients obtained from wavelet analysis are used for training and testing ANN at various distances. This analysis is worked out almost within half cycle. The fault location is carried out for various distances, fault impedance's on 2-bus connected transmission system. A 2-bus transmission system is simulated using simulation software and the analysis of fault is done by wavelet analysis. The proposed wavelet based algorithm is tested for all fault conditions at the faulted area and hence it is proved that the proposed method provided the best results for different fault impedance's, fault generator capacities, fault inception angles (FIA).

articleTitle: Restaurant Reviews Sentimental Analysis Using Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Two prominent machine learning methods applied to sentiment analysis of restaurant reviews they are Logistic Regression and Support Vector Machine (SVM). The dataset comprises 1001 restaurant reviews sourced from Kaggle, classified into positive and negative sentiments based on a numerical scale. Initially, Logistic Regression is used for binary classification and predicting the likelihood of a review being positive or negative. SVM is most widely used algorithms for supervised learning, both linear and non-linear variants, is subsequently employed to optimize classification accuracy by finding hyperplanes that separate classes with maximum margin in feature space. This study aims to compare the effectiveness of these algorithms in discerning sentiment from textual reviews, highlighting their respective strengths and performance outcomes. Experiment results show that the overall accuracy achieved for sentiment classification task using Logistic Regression model is 76.40% and 76.80% in Support Vector Machine.

articleTitle: Multi Agent System Based Control for Energy Management of Hybrid Microgrid System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Microgrids are decentralized power generation systems installed on customer premises, incorporating various capacity generating sets and modes. These systems not only cater to the specific energy needs of the consumer but also contribute excess power back to the main grid. Often integrating renewable sources like solar PV cells, wind energy, and battery energy -storage systems, microgrids have gained global popularity due to their potential for compact size and adaptable configurations. To ensure stable operation amidst the diverse array of power sources, a Multi-Agent System (MAS) is employed. This MAS is specifically designed for modeling and autonomous decision-making. The study concentrates on a microgrid, equipped with 1.5 kW wind energy, 1 kW solar PV power, a battery (24V 150Ah), and a local electrical load. Together, these components develop the Hybrid Microgrid System (HMGS). The simulation design is constructed using the Java Agent Development Environment (JADE), enabling effective management of the heterogeneous system components. The primary objective is to investigate the performance and reliability of the HMGS, with a particular emphasis on the crucial role played by MAS in coordinating the intricate interplay of various power sources to achieve sustainable and efficient operation.

articleTitle: A Fuzzy Approach Towards the Measurement of Subject-Specific Cognitive Load during Mental Task Using Hemodynamic Response
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Every individual exhibits a different cognitive load for a particular task of the same level of difficulty. Measuring the cognitive load of an individual can help to develop an effective learning environment, design personalized learning materials and diagnose specific learning impairments. The primary aim of this study is to measure the subject-specific utilization of cognitive load during the mental arithmetic task using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) signals. For this purpose, we have collected fNIRS signals from fourteen healthy subjects while performing mental arithmetic tasks of three difficulty levels: low, medium and high. Statistical features are extracted from the collected fNIRS signal. After that, a fuzzy classifier has been developed where the fuzzy membership functions for each of the input features are generated using fuzzy c-means clustering. The experimental results show that the subjects undergoing the experiment utilize different levels of cognitive loads for a given task with the same level of difficulty. The proposed model achieves 89.92 % classification accuracy.

articleTitle: RAKTAMITRA- An Alert Centric Blood Donation Initiative
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Blood is a critical component for human health, yet the process of finding blood donors can be time-consuming and inefficient, especially during emergencies. Current methods often involve multiple rounds of communication, which delays the timely procurement of life-saving blood. To address these challenges, we have developed “RAKTAMITRA,” a mobile application designed to streamline the blood donation process. This app connects blood donors with recipients by integrating blood type compatibility and geographical proximity. The key technical components of the application include an intuitive and user-friendly interface developed using Android Studio for cross-platform compatibility on both Android and iOS devices. A robust backend powered by Firebase handles real-time data management and synchronization, storing user information, blood type, and location details securely. The app utilizes Google Maps API for geolocation services, enabling accurate tracking of donor and recipient locations to facilitate proximity-based matching. Additionally, Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) is used to implement the push notification system, ensuring that potential donors are promptly notified of nearby donation requests. Users in urgent need of blood can post their requirements on the app, triggering an instant search for potential donors with matching blood types in their vicinity. Once a match is identified, the app notifies donors based on their location to ensure rapid assistance. The platform employs stringent security measures to protect users' personal information, and admin oversight to monitor and address any inappropriate content or any other activities. “RAKTAMITRA” significantly expedites the blood donation process by leveraging technology to reduce the time and effort needed to locate compatible donors. The integration of blood type and location ensures that help is available swiftly, potentially saving lives in critical moments. The app's secure framework maintains user confidentiality and trust, while the admin oversight ensures a safe and reliable platform for all users. By harnessing the power of technology, “RAKTAMITRA” offers an innovative solution to the challenges of blood donation in emergency healthcare services. It enhances the efficiency and effectiveness of blood donation efforts, making it an indispensable tool for both donors and recipients. This application not only saves time but also improves the overall coordination and reliability of blood donation processes, providing a robust support system in critical healthcare scenarios.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Implementation on SAR Data for Built-Up Extraction: Case Study Hyderabad City
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: India is growing at a speedier pace, and with the largest population in the world as country and of the population is in urban areas, is still growing. As per the 2011 census, 30% of the population resides in urban India, with 8000 cities. To streamline the growth and harness resources, the Indian Government of India has various projects such as AMRUT, Jal Jeevan Mission, Jal Shakti Abhiyan, etc. Monitoring built-up growth through satellite data is vital for regional planning and development. Microwave data has the advantage of day-night acquisition and cloud penetration, which can be exploited for many applications in areas usually covered by clouds. The urban areas, which are growing exponentially, need to be monitored, for which satellite data provides an excellent source because of its temporal coverage. The increasing availability of SAR satellite data using various bands such as C and S from Indian and other satellite missions enables the exploration of the potential of information extraction in different applications such as agriculture, Urban & Infrastructure, etc., While Advancement of data processing techniques, and computational infrastructure enable conceptualize and develop the application based on Deep Learning (DL) techniques in built-up extraction. The current study is conducted to process SAR data from NOVASAR, Sentinnel-1, and EOS 4 satellites using deep learning (DL) techniques that have been used for built-up area extraction. A Dense Neural Network (DNN) based model using Python, Tensor Flow, Keras and GDAL have been used. Hence, the current study aims to develop a Dense Neural Network (DNN) model to extract the built-up areas over Hyderabad, India, from multiple SAR satellite data, i.e., Sentinel-1, NOVASAR and EOS-4, using various polarizations datasets. It is found that EOS-4 datasets gave the best results among the three.

articleTitle: Digital Twin of a 5-Bar Parallel Manipulator with Singularity Avoidance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Digital twin is one of emerging components of Industry 4.0 and it is not so common in the literature. In this project, digital twin of a 5-bar parallel manipulator is modeled. These are very much useful for robotics process automation. This digital twin encompasses the closed-loop constraints of the parallel manipulator, joint limits of the passive joints and the mass and inertia properties of its physical twin and loT communication is established between the physical and digital twins. The digital twin is built on SIMSCAPE multi-body platform. Singularity is the most important aspect of a parallel manipulator to be addressed. In the physical twin, there is an extra actuator provided to take the manipulator outside of singularity configuration. This feature is also included in the digital twin. A Jacobian block is incorporated in the digital twin which calculates the determinant of both forward and inverse Jacobian matrices. When anyone of the Jacobian matrices goes to zero, then the base actuator of the digital twin moves and takes the manipulator outside the singularity configuration. Another feature of the digital twin is lOT control by using ESP8266 module and a ESP32 module by which the data is transferred from the active joints of the physical model to the ThingSpeak cloud platform. This data is then transmitted to the Simscape model using ThingSpeak Input block in MATLAB Simscape.

articleTitle: Music Recommendation System Using Facial Detection Based Emotion Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Music is intrinsically important to humanity due to its significant connections with the brain. Behaviors and emotions of humans are driven by music, which generates a unique sense of unity in the brain. This paper introduces an innovative Music Recommendation System (MRS) that uses real-time face emotion detection to personalize music choices in real-time. The proposed model is based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) in order to recognize emotions from users' facial expressions. The emotions are then combined with a sophisticated music classification system to suggest songs that match the user's current emotional state. To enhance the user experience, user-friendly web application is created for the working of the proposed model. It allows for real-time video feed processing and instant music recommendation updates. Additionally, the system employs emotion music mapping, where musical characteristics such as pitch, tempo, and volume are analysed to correlate specific emotions with appropriate music selections. This study enhances affective computing and music information retrieval by showcasing the effective application of real-time emotion recognition in music recommendation, leading to the development of more intuitive and responsive digital media platforms.

articleTitle: A Reinforcement Learning Sampling Optimization Method Based on Training Value
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has been widely used in various real-world applications, such as robotics, game playing, and finance. However, traditional RL algorithms exhibit limitations in training efficiency and performance. In this paper, we propose a novel RL optimization algorithm based on training value. The proposed algorithm makes use of the training value metric to improve experience sampling and utilization, accelerating the training process and improving the agent's performance in the task. The algorithm calculates training value by considering the TD error of experience data, and prioritizes experience with high training value during training. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm through experiments on multiple Atari game environments. Compared to traditional prioritized experience replay (PER) and baseline DQN algorithms, the proposed algorithm achieves comparable or better average reward in most environments and significantly reduces the training time. These results suggest that the proposed training value-based optimization method can effectively improve the performance of RL algorithms and can be a promising approach for future RL research.

articleTitle: Frequency Domain Parameters of a Two-Area Automatic Generation Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: During the dynamic operation of a power system, unpredictable changes in load result in deviations in both frequency and voltage from their intended levels, posing challenges such as line tripping and the threat of blackouts. To address these issues, the implementation of automatic generation control is es-sential, which comprises two critical components: load frequency control (LFC) and an automatic voltage regulator (AVR). This study aims to delve into the exploration of adjustments in the system dynamics of a two-area load-frequency control system. The investigation entails analyzing modifications in the bode diagram caused by fluctuations in PID controller parameters. The variations in frequency domain parameters were identified and examined both with and without control.

articleTitle: License Plate Recognition and IOT based Parking System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The demand for parking increases day by day as the rise of automobile utility increases with population. The proposed automated parking system is a significant advancement in parking space management, reducing the need for manual intervention. It utilizes LPR technology to accurately detect and identify vehicle license plates, streamlining the parking process. Unlike current systems that rely on lifts and manual parking maneuvers with trained staff, our innovative solution seamlessly identifies vehicles and assigns parking slots upon entry through the organization's designated entrance. When IoT sensors and cameras are integrated, they eliminate the need for parking attendants and empowers drivers to easily locate their parking spots. Furthermore, the system maintains a comprehensive database of parking slot occupancy, facilitating convenient vehicle retrieval. In summary, this automated parking system enhances operational efficiency and user experience, offering a secure, efficient, and forward-looking approach to parking space management in diverse organizations.

articleTitle: Stock Price Prediction Leveraging News Headlines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Predicting stock prices remains a challenging task in the financial and trading industries due to the high volatility and complex dependencies involved. Traditional methods such as ARIMA models have been supplemented by deep learning techniques, including hybrid neural network models, to improve forecasting accuracy. Recent research has explored incorporating diverse data sources, such as sentiment analysis from social media, Google Trends data, and news headlines, to enhance predictive models. This paper introduces a multivariate approach that integrates news headlines with stock price data to predict future stock prices. The challenge of data collection is addressed by scraping news headlines and cleaning the data using trans-former models. The processed news data is then combined with stock price data obtained from Yahoo Finance's API. A stacked multivariate LSTM model is trained on this combined dataset for stock price prediction. While existing literature offers numerous models for time series analysis and some for predicting stock movement, research on incorporating news headlines for stock price prediction remains limited. This paper attempts to fill this gap by leveraging news information to enrich the deep learning model. The paper reviews existing works in time series analysis, describes the data acquisition and processing techniques, explains the LSTM model architecture for stock price prediction with news headlines, presents experimental results, and concludes with insights and future directions.

articleTitle: Harmonizing Individual and Group Interests: A Strategy for Fostering Cooperation in Social Dilemma Games
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Why humans cooperate remains an open question. Researchers use social dilemma games to try and find some answers. Unfortunately, over the last 3 decades arguably only slow progress has been made. This is due to a reliance on just fitness to evolve strategies which removes any player decision process. In this paper, we propose a new approach to evolving strategies in social dilemma games. This approach combines individual interests with group interests and injects a formal decision process into strategy selection. It combines the ideas of Adam Smith, the father of modern economics, and the work of Nobel laureate Lloyd Shapley. Our results from public goods game experiments show our approach can produce dramatically different strategy evolution but one which matches player preferences. This new approach provides a better framework for investigating cooperation in human populations.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Clinical and Sociodemographic Data on Congenital Syphilis Using Gaussian Naive Bayes and XAI Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: This research delves into the pressing public health issue of congenital syphilis in Pernambuco, Brazil, using machine learning and sophisticated data analysis techniques. Leveraging a vast dataset from the Mae Coruja Pernambucana Program, covering a decade from 2013 to 2022 with 47,604 records, the study aims to pinpoint crucial risk factors linked to congen-ital syphilis and devise effective strategies for public health interventions. Central to the analysis is the utilization of the Gaussian Naive Bayes classification algorithm, known for its simplicity and efficiency in managing vast datasets. The model's effectiveness was assessed using conventional criteria, revealing an impressive accuracy of 97 %, precision of 98 %, recall of 99%, and an Fl score of 99%. These measurements demon-strate the model's outstanding capacity to accurately detect cases of congenital syphilis while reducing the occurrence of false positives and negatives, a critical aspect in the realm of public health. Moreover, the study employs Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), specifically the Local Interpretable Model- agnostic Explanations (LIME) technique, to provide clarity on the decision-making process of the model. A key finding from the feature importance analysis was the prominence of the “MOTHER_SYPHILIS_TEST_RESULT” variable. This variable emerged as a significant predictor, indicating that the syphilis test results of mothers are crucial in predicting congenital syphilis in newborns. In summary, the study demonstrates how the utilization of machine learning and explainable AI, particularly Gaussian Naive Bayes and LIME, efficiently identifies crucial predictors of congenital syphilis, resulting in enhanced and actionable public health interventions.

articleTitle: High-Level Synthesis Based Hardware Accelerator for LSTM Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is a kind of Recurrent Neural Network known for capturing long-term de-pendencies in sequence prediction tasks. However, the processing in a LSTM network includes several compute intensive tasks such as matrix-vector multiplication, array-oriented addition and multiplication, which take up a significant amount of time and memory. To address this challenge, a unique hardware design can be custom-built. This paper introduces a hardware accelerator designed for LSTM operations. To minimize the memory usage, a Bank-wise structured weight pruning method is proposed. An optimized algorithm is employed to enable faster computation of Sparse-Matrix Dense-Vector multiplication, which reduced the number of computations by more than 50%. RTL for proposed algorithm is synthesized using Vitis High-level Synthesis tool. The C++ code is made efficient by the optimization directives, which support loop pipelining and unrolling. The design is analyzed using benchmarking IMDB trained data obtained from TensorFlow model for Sentiment Analysis on Zynq 7000-SoC. With a smaller amount of resources usage, our model achieved an accuracy of 92.59 %.

articleTitle: Enhanced Multi-Class Weather Image Classification Using Data Augmentation and Dynamic Learning on Pre-Trained Deep Neural Net
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The present work employs the VGG16 deep neural network as a foundational model for weather image classification. Experiments have been carried out on a Weather Phenomena Dataset (WEAPD) having 11 distinct classes. The article exploits data augmentation along with suitable hyperparameter tuning (specifically using dynamic learning rate) on transfer learnt VGG16. An overall best accuracy of 92.10% establishes the effectiveness of the proposed method. The performance of the proposed strategy is also compared with those of the state-of-the-art methods. This research contributes in advancing the understanding and accuracy of weather event classification, holding potential implications for various applications in meteorology and related fields.

articleTitle: Advanced Threat Protection for File Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Cloud storage is widely used in various industries, but concerns about data security persist. Traditional techniques like cryptography and steganography have limitations and cannot provide sufficient security on their own. To address this issue, we propose a unique security system that combines multiple cryptographic algorithms and steganography. By using fast and secure symmetric key algorithms, such as AES and DES, along with the benefits of the asymmetric key algorithm RSA, we develop an efficient method to encrypt and decrypt data. This approach takes advantage of the strengths of each algorithm to create a strong encryption system that protects data from unauthorized access. Furthermore, incorporating splitting and merging techniques adds an extra layer of security. The LSB steganography technique is used to securely store essential key information. Implementing this comprehensive approach in the cloud environment not only enhances server security but also builds user confidence, as encrypted data is stored on a single cloud server. Overall, this sophisticated security mechanism offers enhanced data protection, making cloud storage a more reliable and secure option for various applications in different industries.

articleTitle: Self-Organizing Map for Automated Quality Assessment in Algorithmic Music Computation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: This work explores the application of Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) to the domain of algorithmic music creation, performing the role of the most critical element in the creation process, namely, automated quality assessment of the music under composition. Leveraging principles from Rasa theory, which emphasizes the emotional and aesthetic dimensions of universal human experience, our study introduces a novel approach to compose music using specific aspects of Evolutionary Algorithms. It aims to generate music aligned with each of four important Rasas, which will elicit the specific human emotions associated with that Rasa. This innovative approach aims to bridge the gap between computational creativity and human perception, providing a valuable understanding for musicians, composers, and researchers in the field of music. The prime challenge is to synthesize a Fitness Function (FF) that can accurately detect the “degree of adherence” of the composition to the targeted Rasa. Computational results presented here demonstrate the surprising effectiveness of our approach of taking Self-Organizing Map as FF in capturing the intricacies of Rasa classification, over other established and popular approaches.

articleTitle: Real-Time Detection of Speech based Affective Behaviour using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Identification of human emotions is for various reasons like knowing one's mindset and communicating needs and opinions. Uttered speech and facial images can be used to identify the variations of these expressions. This research embarks on a comprehensive journey into Speech Emotion Recognition, aimed at understanding human emotions such as ‘anger’, ‘calm’, ‘surprise’, ‘sadness’, ‘happiness’, ‘fear’, ‘disgust’, and many more. Utilizing cutting-edge deep learning methodologies across diverse static datasets like CREMA-D, RAVDESS, SAVEE, and TESS, explored the nuanced intricacies of emotion detection. Delved into augmentation techniques, enriching the different stages like data wrangling, feature extraction, training and testing with the perception of exactly how synthetic data can enhance model performance. The process emerged employing a deep learning method using a ‘Convolutional Neural Network’ including resources for data collection, preliminary modelling, design, training, analysis, and orientation to potential applications. The appropriate modelling of convolution, pooling, and global layers along with the tuning of hyperparameters of the network gave results that match the features of diverse emotions including changes in ‘zero crossing rate’, ‘energy’, ‘entropy’, ‘spectral’ and ‘cepstral’ features. The model achieved the best performance considering the diversity and complexity of the static data with an overall accurateness of 90% when tested on the trained dataset compared to 84% when determined on real-time speech. There was observed constantly high value of Precision, recall, and F1 scores across multiple categories; this demonstrated the robustness of the model and its general capabilities across the traditional approach of speech emotion recognition.

articleTitle: Meta-Heuristic-Based Feature Selection for Stroke Prediction in Smart Healthcare System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The paper introduces an approach for enhanced feature selection using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Moth-Flame Optimization (MFO) in conjunction with Artificial Neural Network (ANN) as the classifier for stroke detection. The feature subsets are adjusted dynamically with PSO + MFO, resulting in the optimization of the classifier's performance for quick and accurate detection. The proposed approach employs PSO's exploration capabilities and MFO's probabilistic updates for exploring the solution space. The ANN classifier is trained on the resultant selected features subset, and three optimizers are used, namely, Adam, RMSprop, and Adadelta, separately. The model's performance is evaluated by plotting training and validation accuracy loss curves and accuracy curves using three optimizers. By proposing this model, we aim to offer a robust solution for a highly efficient stroke detection system in a smart healthcare system.

articleTitle: A Framework for Visualization of Streaming 3D Point Cloud
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: With the rapid development of 3D acquisition technologies, 3D sensors are becoming increasingly available and affordable, including various types of 3D scanners, LiDAR, and RGB-D cameras. Point cloud data can be extracted from different sensors according to specific requirements. A framework is developed to visualize live Streaming of real time objects as point clouds by using Intel RealSense Camera. This framework displays 3D point cloud data and performs various operations on the data by acquiring control of the point cloud data (operations such as rotating in different directions, depth sensing, controlling the movement of the point cloud) using computer vision. The main goal of this project is to stream 3D objects in real time which helps in application of detection of objects while traveling, surveillance, etc.

articleTitle: Smart Garbage Classification Using Cutting Edge Technology (VGG-16)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: This paper introduces a pioneering system for automated garbage classification, integrating deep learning techniques and chatbot functionality to revolutionize waste management practices. Leveraging OpenCV and live video streaming from an IP webcam, our system captures images of diverse garbage types. Employing the VGG-16 model and a custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), it achieves real-time classification of 12 distinct categories of garbage, with results promptly displayed. Additionally, all processed images are logged in an Excel spreadsheet, enabling seamless integration with a trained chatbot capable of addressing user queries regarding garbage classification and recycling options. This symbiotic integration enhances system functionality and user engagement. Experimental validation showcases the system's remarkable accuracy, achieving a classification rate of 96%. Our approach promises to significantly improve waste management efficiency and promote sustainable practices.

articleTitle: Navigating Financial Markets: Exploring Advanced Neural Networks for Stock Price Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The stock market serves as a complex financial ecosystem, where diverse methodologies are employed to forecast price movements. This paper centers on the technical analysis of stock markets, exploring a range of models categorized into statistical, machine learning, and deep learning paradigms. Utilizing the Nifty BeES dataset, a pivotal ETF index fund in India, we conduct a comparative analysis of moving averages and LSTM models, evaluating their performance through metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). We then propose a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) architecture which outperforms all other models in stock price prediction. Distinguished by its ability of time mixing and feature mixing attributes, the MLP demonstrates superior efficacy compared to conventional deep learning models. Looking ahead, we propose integrating sentiment analysis into our predictive framework to capture market sentiments and further enhance forecasting accuracy. This research underscores the significance of leveraging advanced methodologies to navigate the complexities of the stock market. By refining predictive models and incorporating market sentiments, we aim to equip investors with actionable insights for informed decision-making in dynamic financial landscapes.

articleTitle: Exploring Students' Attitudes Towards Robotics Technology in STEM Education: A Machine Learning-Based Prediction Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to predict the extent to which students will accept robotics technology in future teaching plans. The study involves students engaging in a two-week project-based learning program on robotics technology, after which they will decide whether it is suitable for them. To achieve this, the paper uses several prediction algorithms based on Machine Learning (ML), including Linear Regression (LR), Ridge Regression (RR), Elastic Net (EN) regression, and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) models. The sample group consists of 35 students from STEM high schools in Egypt. The research findings indicate that the students have gained confidence and satisfaction in robotics technology and believe it will have significant value in the future. The prediction results obtained from the ML regression models support these findings. The dataset used in the study includes seven input features and one target output representing the total prediction values of accepting and rejecting robotics technology in STEM schools. The regression models LR, RR, EN, and KNN achieve determination coefficients (R2) of 99.99%, 98.80%,99.20%, and 85.60%, respectively.

articleTitle: Enhancing Student Model via Knowledge Transfer with Prior-Informed Constraints from a Teacher
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: We introduce a prior-informed teacher network with a constraint loss for knowledge transfer to enhance deep learning models' efficiency in image classification tasks. Our approach accelerates the student model's performance and achieves a faster convergence replicating the behavior of a constraint teacher model. The teacher model transfers knowledge through a distillation process. To enhance knowledge quality, we integrate total variation (TV) loss and a newly introduced high-intensity penalty into the teacher model's loss function. TV loss promotes smooth, coherent feature maps by reducing noise and preserving structural details and the high-intensity penalty ensures stable and consistent predictions by penalizing overly confident misclassifications and bringing those predictions closer to the boundary values. Thus the combined loss function acts as a regularizer for the teacher model and helps in making the predictions softer. The student model reached 74.21 % accuracy after three epochs and 79.35% by the end of training, surpassing the baseline model's 68.54% and 74.3% on CIFAR-10. Additionally, it demonstrated superior performance on the more complex CIFAR-100 dataset. The proposed technique was also seen to be outperforming other state-of-the-art knowledge distillation approaches.

articleTitle: Efficient Lightweight Blockchain-based Authentication and Intrusion Detection System for Secure Message Transfer in VANETs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Securing the transfer of messages is a challenging task for communication between vehicles in Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks (VANETs). The effectiveness of vehicle-to-vehicle communication is of top priority in VANETs, where the lives and possessions of drivers are at stake. The ultimate objective of a vehicle network is to ensure fast and proper broadcasting of information concerning life-threatening incidents, such as traffic jams and accident reports. However, these messages are prone to attacks by misleading intruders attempting to modify or alter them during communication. Emergency communications are basically segregated on the basis of the message schema and safety level, primarily due to the lack of quick and reliable communication and the need to detect attacks. This paper proposes an efficient lightweight blockchain-based authentication system for the secure transfer of emergency messages in Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks (VANETs). The main objectives are to develop an intrusion detection system for V2V communication using machine learning techniques and to use a lightweight Rivest-Shamir-Adleman(RSA) technique with three prime integers to ensure authentication. Additionally, Ganache and Ethereum blockchain technologies are utilized to create a secure message storage and retrieval system. The proposed system demonstrates improved encryption and decryption times and enhanced attack detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhanced Pneumonia Detection In Chest X-Rays Through Model Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The accurate detection of pneumonia using chest X-rays is crucial for rapid medical treatment. Despite advancement, achieving high accuracy and recall rates remains challenging due to the complexity of image processing and data imbalance. In this paper, we propose a novel ensemble model for pneumonia detection that utilizes concatenation, averaging, and weighted averaging techniques. Using pretrained models like VGG19, InceptionV3, and Vision Transformer, our method delivers impressive precision (0.9861), recall (0.9813), F1 score (0.9816), and accuracy (0.9899). Interestingly, the concatenation technique surpasses all metrics. We address the issue of data imbalance by merging two standard datasets, which improves the robustness of our technique. Comparative research demonstrates that our technology is superior than existing methods. Our results highlight the value of curated datasets in healthcare research and show how ensemble learning may improve the accuracy of pneumonia diagnosis.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection Using Deep Learning and VGG-16 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Brain tumors are defined by the unchecked proliferation of cells, resulting in the formation of atypical tissues. Segmentation is utilized to separate tumor regions in the brain, and deep learning is widely employed to address this challenge. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model framework with appropriate training parameters is constructed in this study using the Visual Geometry Group (VGG 16) for brain tumor diagnosis. VGG 16, renowned for its efficiency and ease of use, is utilized as one of the primary CNN models. We also design an effective method for brain tumor detection using MRI, enabling fast and precise decision-making. Based on the VGG 16 base network, the improved CNN creates convolutional feature maps and categorizes them to find possible tumor locations. We evaluate the suggested methodology's on various types of MRI brain images, such as benign tumors, malignant tumors, and pituitary tumors. Our method surpasses traditional methods and achieves a precision of 98 %, an F -1 score of 99 %, a recall of 99%, and an overall accuracy of 99.15%.

articleTitle: GesturesSpeak: An IoT-Based Gesture to Speech Translator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Hand gestures serve as a natural and intuitive means for humans to communicate ideas and intents. For people with speaking or hearing disabilities, sign languages based on visual hand gestures are indispensable for their expression. With recent advances in machine perception and proliferation of Internet-of- Things (IoT) devices, automating gesture recognition to generate textual or speech output has transformative potential to augment accessibility. This paper surveys key innovations in gesture- to-text conversion spanning machine learning, deep learning and IoT-driven approaches. The research first motivate the assistive technology applications of an IoT framework leveraging specialized sensors and edge devices for gesture tracking, coupled with intelligent algorithms to interpret gestures and convert them into language. Our study covers convolutional and recurrent neural networks for spatial and temporal modelling, as well as multimodal fusion techniques. Challenges related to occlusion, sensor constraints and model generalization are discussed. The paper highlights the tremendous value of gesture-driven systems in enabling more immersive human-computer interaction and accessible interfaces for diverse communities.

articleTitle: Analyzing Computer Virus Propagation: Integrating Monte Carlo Simulations with Delay Differential Equation Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The widespread digitization of essential services has made the internet a prime target for large-scale cyber attacks, despite efforts to bolster security measures. Today's organizations face a balancing act between securing networks and managing operational costs. Existing models often overlook the effectiveness of security techniques and fail to capture the varying risk levels across network paths. In this paper we explore the dynamics of computer virus propagation through the lens of a delay differential equation model, specifically the SEIRS model. Utilizing Monte Carlo simulations, the authors investigate virus spread within a compartmental framework. Furthermore, stability analysis of the model is undertaken to comprehend the factors that influence the persistence of the virus. The obtained results are illustrated through various graphs.

articleTitle: AcuLearn - Precision Based Learning Analytics Platform Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: In today's world, the use of data analytics with precision has been extremely important and crucial with the changing times. The creation of virtual environments to facilitate communication and education among the students and teach-ers alike. It allows the creation of personalized education for students. Machine Learning algorithms, hence can be helpful to recommend students to what courses that can be taken and their likely improvement of the system. This study shows the creation of an website for creating better personalized education for students including course completion predictors and score predictors to help them make decisions proactively. The system shows the random forest regression for score prediction and random forest classifier for course completion to perform the best among all such algorithms.

articleTitle: Comparative study of different LLM's for Captioning Images to Help Blind People
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The proposed system leverages LLMs, including GPT2, DistillGPT2, BERT, and RoBERTa, to provide detailed scene descriptions for the visually impaired. It employs an Encoder-Decoder architecture, with the Vision Transformer as the encoder and a distilled GPT-2 model as the decoder, facilitating the generation of comprehensive image captions. Training used a diverse dataset of around a hundred thousand samples on hardware equipped with an Nvidia Tesla V100 PCIE card and two Intel Xeon Silver CPUs. The model achieved a ROUGE score of 21.69%, signifying its potential to generate captions closely resembling human descriptions after training on suitable LLMs in the near future. This research has profound implications for enhancing the independence, education, and employment prospects of the visually impaired.

articleTitle: A Survey on Multi-Classification of Pulmonary Diseases Using Image Processing and Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Multi-classification of pulmonary diseases poses a significant challenge, particularly when diseases share similar radiological presentations like lung cancer, pneumonia, and COVID-19. While chest CT scan images are essential for diagnosis, manual interpretation by radiologists is time-consuming and difficult, even for experts. Deep learning algorithms offer promise in this domain, demonstrating high accuracy in classifying these diseases from CT images. This review examines recent advances in using deep learning for multiclassification of pulmonary diseases. It discusses various preprocessing techniques, deep learning architectures to enhance model performance. Additionally, a comparative analysis of different deep learning models on publicly available CT datasets is presented. The findings suggest that deep learning models could serve as valuable tools for multiclassification of pulmonary diseases, potentially improving diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. Nonetheless, further research is required to develop and validate these models on large, diverse datasets and ensure their robustness in real-world clinical settings.

articleTitle: Understanding Student Behavior and Learning Patterns through Video Analysis: A Comprehensive Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Technology-enhanced learning (TEL) has emerged as a powerful approach to facilitate and enhance learning experiences in diverse educational settings. The integration of TEL tools enables the collection of real-time and longitudinal data. Technology-enhanced learning provides the digital infrastructure and tools that enable educators to collect and process diverse data. It is fundamental for successfully implementing Multi-modal Learning Analytics (MMLA) in understanding student learning patterns. This literature paper presents a comprehensive review of research at the intersection of MMLA, video analytics, human gesture, and their relation to behavior and learning patterns. This study explores how video analysis techniques capture and analyze human gestures, revealing insights into underlying behavioral dynamics and learning patterns. This study conducts a scoping review of relevant literature from diverse fields such as computer science, education, human-computer interaction, and medical science. The authors utilized LitMap, a comprehensive search strategy to identify pertinent literature. In education context, understanding the role of gestures in learning can inform the development of instructional strategies that optimize knowledge acquisition and retention. By studying patterns in human gestures and behavior, particularly in the education context, researchers can gain insights into students' engagement, cognitive processes, and learning strategies. This scoping review presents an in-depth survey of research encompassing video analytics, human gestures, and their interplay with behavior and learning patterns. The study delves into the behavioral factors that impact student learning and explores how educators can leverage them to enhance their teaching practices.

articleTitle: Traffic Congestion Management Using Deep Reinforcement Learning and Decentralized Routing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Traffic congestion management and routing of vehicles are interdependent problems. The performance of the problems depends on how well these problems learn about the behaviours of one another. In this paper, we propose centralized traffic congestion management where a grid agent recommends speed limits for the road segments based on the measured traffic volume whereas the vehicles perform decentralized routing and speed selection based on recommendations. The objective of the congestion management problem is to maximize the expected sum utility of the heterogeneous vehicles which traverse the links managed by the grid agent. The problem of congestion management is formulated as a deep reinforcement learning problem which is solved using the deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm. The objective of any vehicle is to select the fastest path suitable for its travel requirement. Using real-world traffic datasets, we analyze the performance of the grid agent and the vehicles in terms of the expected total utility of the vehicles and the mean link congestion. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms a greedy method and a random method.

articleTitle: A Survey on Applications and Performance of Deep Convolution Neural Network Architecture for Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Image segmentation constitutes a critical component within the realm of medical image processing and analysis, bearing profound implications on treatment efficacy and patient survival rates. This technique serves as a foundational preprocessing step, facilitating the partitioning of images into meaningful structures or components pivotal for object representation, detection, recognition, measurement, and visualization. Given its paramount significance, a plethora of research endeavors have been dedicated to this domain, yielding a myriad of segmentation approaches predicated on intensity, color, texture, and other modalities. Numerous computational paradigms encompassing supervised, unsupervised, parametric, and probabilistic region-based techniques have emerged in pursuit of refining segmentation accuracy and efficiency. Of late, the landscape has witnessed a surge in leveraging machine learning methodologies, particularly deep learning utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs), to develop robust and automated image segmentation models. This paper eschews conventional segmentation strategies, instead focusing squarely on scrutinizing deep neural convolution networks and their variants for automated image segmentation. By delving into the state-of-the-art algorithms proposed between 2015 and 2017, we meticulously assess their efficacy, performance, advantages, and limitations vis-à-vis prevailing research challenges and objectives. Through this critical evaluation, we discern nuanced insights into the current state of affairs, identifying gaps, limitations, and potential avenues for advancement. By juxtaposing contemporary methodologies against the backdrop of evolving research paradigms, we offer a comprehensive delineation of the landscape's trajectory, thereby elucidating the future scope and imperatives for further advancement.

articleTitle: Enhancing Image Super-Resolution with GANs Featuring Enhanced Deep Super-Resolution and Attention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Improving the quality and resolution of low- resolution digital images is an important task with far-reaching implications for a variety of applications, including medical imaging, surveillance, and content retrieval. To solve the high- resolution problem of a single image, this study proposes a new Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) model that includes an Enhanced Deep Super-Resolution (EDSR) generator. Our model includes a sensitivity function and a Squeeze-and- Excitation (SE) block in an EDSR design. These SE blocks directly model channel connections to optimize channel-specific performance responses and improve network capabilities without incurring significant computational costs. After extensive training using complex data processing methods such as rotation, rotation, and rotation, our model shows an impressive ability to enhance image details and traditional culture more accurately. Our strategy outperforms existing models both statistically and qualitatively with better signal-to- noise ratios (PSNRs) on the DIV2K dataset. These results, together with deep learning models, demonstrate the role of attentional processes in improving image resolution and lay the groundwork for further work in this field.

articleTitle: A Study on Sustainable Tourism and Application of Sentiment Analysis in the Tourism Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Sentiment analysis has emerged as one of the most promising tools for analyzing the travelers review about the various facilities related to the tourism industry, be it a choice of right destination, hotels, travel agencies, airlines or any other mode of transportation etc., helping the tourist to opt for the sustainable and green tourism initiatives. Sentiment analysis facilitates the identification and extraction of subjective data from texts, including attitudes, sentiments, andfeelings. Some of the approaches used by sentiment analysis are lexicon-based approaches, machine learning algorithms, and deep learning models for checking the polarity of the comments. The authors explore the multifaceted applications of sentiment analysis in the tourism industry. Through the examination of traveler reviews, social media exchanges, and online conversations, sentiment analysis offers priceless insights into travelers' opinions, preferences, and degrees of satisfaction to the stake holders in the tourism industry. The study also focused on how sentiment analysis can help in implementing the sustainable practices. The findings of the study will enable stakeholders in the tourism sector to make informed decisions, enhance customer experiences, and foster a culture of sustainability within the industry.

articleTitle: Unstructured to Visualized: Transforming Data into Knowledge Graphs via Processing Pipeline
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: As the amount of unstructured data increases at a significant rate, the task of extracting useful and valuable data becomes challenging. In this paper, two novel state-of-the-art pipelines for relation extraction from unstructured textual data are presented using ML and NLP approaches. Each pipeline has three modules including coreference resolution, named entity linking, and relationship extraction. This study is based on a Netflix dataset, the relations derived from this dataset are then used to build a recommendation system. The first pipeline employs rule-based RE, while the second implements a sophisticated REBEL model to extract relations. After evaluating their performance and efficacy, the best of the pipeline is used to create a movie-based recommendation system employing Neo4j to store relations and similarity scored from the description.

articleTitle: Content Retrieval in Information Centric Networks Using Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: In Information Centric Network (ICN) consumer generates an interest packet to retrieve data. The intermediate nodes forwards interest packet to reach content location. The ICN does not use any intelligence in forwarding interest. In this paper, an intelligent forwarding scheme is proposed based on Machine Learning (ML). For that, a routing and forwarding dataset derived from simulated ICN topology is used. In the first stage, a Content Routers (CRs) are trained using ML models. Then, CRs use the acquired knowledge to forward future interest packets. It is found that the use of ML significantly improves the performance in terms of retrieval time and network throughput. The said dataset is created from a simulation scenario designed in ndnSim-2.0. Eighteen models are used in predicting the content location. The experimental evaluation reveals that the Extra Tree (ET), Random Forest (RF), and Decision Tree (DT) perform with 98% accuracy. The results of the machine model were verified by creating a random ICN topology and examining the success rate for ML-guided interest forwarding. A comparison is made with forwarding techniques with and without using ML techniques. In comparison to non-ML variations, ML-guided forwarding techniques perform better in content retrieval with nearly 20% improvement in performance.

articleTitle: Fruit Classification Based On Freshness
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Fruit freshness detection is critical in the food industry for maintaining quality, minimizing waste, and meeting consumer expectations. As the global population grows, preserving fruit freshness is increasingly vital. This project introduces an AI system that identifies fruit types and assesses their freshness using color, texture, and other visual attributes. The system employs Agile methodology and machine learning techniques, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), separating classification and freshness detection models to handle various fruits under different conditions. Achieving over 90% accuracy and rapid classification, the system works from any device with an internet connection, offering significant benefits to producers and consumers. The use of transfer learning with the VGG16 model and data augmentation techniques highlights the practical application of deep learning. This system enhances operational efficiency in retail, storage, and personal use. Future work will address system limitations by expanding the dataset, improving real-world utility, boosting accuracy with advanced techniques, and incorporating real-time monitoring features.

articleTitle: Autonomous Vehicle Lane Following Network based on Multimodal Sensor Fusion and LiDAR Reconstruction in Extreme Lighting and Snowing Environments
