publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The self-driving car industry is gaining attention for its role in motion planning technology. Deep learning approaches have been implemented to plan autonomous vehicles' motion, but their effectiveness depends on the data used in training. Despite advancements, fully autonomous vehicles still face limitations, such as lighting-related issues affecting camera image accuracy, and LiDARs are negatively impacted by challenging weather circumstances like snow in varied snowfall conditions, thus becoming imperative to precisely control the motion of the Autonomous Vehicle. To address this, an architecture based on deep-learning networks is proposed for lane-following on roads, consisting of LiDAR De-snowing, Multi-modal Sensor Fusion, VGG16, and gated recurrent units (GRUs). The Point Reconstruction Network (PR-Net) rebuilds points from neighbors, while the Reconstruction Difficulty Network forecasts reconstruction difficulty. Radar measurements and de-snowed LiDAR point clouds are projected onto the front-view image plane, fed into VGG16 and GRU output layers, and processed into two fully connected layers for steering and speed parameters estimation.

articleTitle: Formulating Explainable UI/UX for Bank ATM and Analytic Performance of HCI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: ATM or Automatic Teller Machine is widely adopted worldwide for extending banking services to users on an anywhere - anytime basis. Despite the growth of mobile money transfer apps like Google Pay, PhonePe and Paytm, the ATM services suite is still regarded as a popular mode for multilingual, hard and e - cash transactions in most developing nations mainly due to limited digital literacy. The ATM nodes typically comprise of hardware User Interface (UI) supported by bank server to provide real - time transactions for users. Ironically, there has not been much enhancement in ATM UI/UX for weak users such as - rural, elderly, laborers and other novice users. This paper proposes a novel UI framework in English language to enhance the operational UX in terms of interpretability and inclusion of weak users for Indian banks. This work proposes Explainable UI or XUI which is AI enabled ATM UI that interacts flexibly and effectively with the user, generalizing the UI menu for both weak and existing users. It aims to make Cash Withdrawal and Balance Check, the two most frequently performed operations, easily interpretable or explainable besides other enhancements that reduce latency and improve security. The main contributions of this work are as follows: XUI ATM client for Cash Withdrawal and Balance Check, enhancing ATM security and novel analytic performance index for HCI.

articleTitle: A Novel Attention Informed Voting Ensemble Framework for Retinal Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Retinal diseases poses a considerable hurdle in the field of ophthalmology, requiring precise and effective categorization for prompt diagnosis and treatment. The integration of deep learning in the classification of retinal diseases not only boosts diagnostic accuracy but also aids in early detection and intervention, hence making a significant contribution to enhancing patient care and outcomes. In this investigation, a novel method for an automated classification of retinal diseases through the use of a voting ensemble model is examined. The idea of the classifier is to use both spatial and attentional features by employing two models: Vision Transformer and ResNet-101. The utilization of deep learning methodologies in this particular aspect addresses complexity and variations of retinal images for enhanced identification of various pathological conditions. In this context, the modified MURED dataset with 22 retinal diseases for the numerous trials carried out by the proposed model suggested ensemble model and aimed high-end performance with 87% test accuracy.

articleTitle: Multimodal MRI Analysis for Schizophrenia Classification Using Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Schizophrenia is a complicated mental condition marked by disruptions in thought processes, perceptions, and emotional responses, which can lead to severe social and occupational failure. Structural Magnetic Resonance Imaging (sMRI) and resting-state Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (rs-fMRI) provide useful information about the neuroanatomical and functional changes associated with schizophrenia. This paper presents a unique approach to diagnosing schizophrenia by extracting energy, mean, and variance features from both sMRI and rs-fMRI data. Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm is used to conduct binary classification on sMRI -derived and rs-fMRI -derived features. sMRI -derived features detect dimensional structural variations in brain anatomy, whereas fMRI -derived features show dynamic functional activity patterns over time. Preliminary results show that both modalities have promising discriminating power, with fMRI -derived features outperforming sMRI-derived features. On a cohort of 106 schizophrenia patients and 160 healthy controls, our proposed technique achieved 93.5 % and 95.6 % classification accuracy for sMRI and rs-fMRI data, respectively. The classification accuracies from both modalities are compared to determine their diagnostic usefulness for schizophrenia. Integrating both modalities has the potential to improve the sensitivity and specificity of diagnostic algorithms for schizophrenia, resulting in better clinical results and customized treatment methods. These findings highlight the significance of multimodal MRI methods in schizophrenia diagnosis,

articleTitle: A Novel Low-Complexity Approach to Drowsiness detection Using One Bit Bayes Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The increasing complexity of real-world applications, particularly in the areas of advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and drive safety features, has heightened the search for effective mathematical techniques. The existing research on AI classifiers in this field has not focused on developing a low-complexity system with a high level of accuracy. Instead, researchers are pursuing two distinct approaches: improving accuracy and reducing system complexity. As a result, highly accurate systems are becoming increasingly heavy, while lightweight models are demonstrating decreasing accuracy. In this paper, a novel low-complexity approach is presented which is based on naive bayes classifier that outperforms multiple neural network-based models in terms of computational complexity and outperforms existing mathematical methods in terms of computational speed and predictive accuracy. Leveraging a unique combination of Logarithmic Image Processing (LIP), Gabor filters and One Bit Bayes Classifier (OBBaC), the method demonstrates superior performance in handling complex data sets, containing déclassé images, captured even during dark hours. Through extensive comparative analysis and empirical evaluations, we showcase the remarkable efficiency and efficacy of the proposed approach. Our findings highlight the potential of this method to reacquaint the significance of mathematical modeling of classifiers, providing an accuracy up to 98.17% and improving speed and computational complexity at least by a factor of 2.32×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Automated Hardware Security Evaluation Framework Using PSO and CNN for Optimizing Key Gate Placement and Enhanced Security Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The increasing of integrated circuits complications and the increasing prevalence of third-party manufacturing facilities have led to growing concerns about the security of hardware systems. To prevent third-party attacks, the LL technique has shown promise by inserting additional Key Gates (KG) into a circuit to obscure the original output. However, manual identification of optimal KG locations is time-consuming and suboptima1. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an automated hardware security evaluation framework by integrating Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for placement of KGs, along with an enhanced security analysis using a multi-function gate-based LL technique. The PSO algorithm optimizes KG placement, while the CNN analyses circuit topology to identify the areas where KGs would be most effective. Experimental results on circuits of the ISCAS benchmark demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves maximum security with minimal overhead in area, delay, and power due to KG insertion and replacement. The proposed framework offers an efficient and comprehensive approach to enhance hardware security, enabling designers to evaluate and select the most suitable security techniques for their specific hardware systems. The use of PSO and CNN for automated KG placement reduces the time and effort required for manual placement, while improving the overall security of the hardware.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Dive into Predicting Pneumonia Disease Using ANN and CNN Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Pneumonia is a potentially severe respiratory infection that gradually damages the lungs and can even lead to fatalities. Employing X-ray technology for pneumonia diagnosis can facilitate early detection of this disease. In the contemporary era, artificial intelligence (AI) has brought about substantial transformations in the field of medicine. Consequently, we have developed a deep-learning model specifically designed to diagnose X-ray images. To enhance accessibility and convenience, we have also designed a user-friendly web interface. This platform allows individuals without specialized medical knowledge to upload their X-ray images and gain insights into their health condition. The advantage of this web-based system is its accessibility from virtually anywhere, providing an initial point of assessment before consulting a healthcare professional. Moreover, this approach significantly reduces the time required for diagnosis, which is especially beneficial for those residing in remote areas. Additionally, it offers a cost-effective alternative for medical evaluation, thus contributing positively to our society. In the present scenario, where timely identification of diseases is often hindered by insufficient awareness and knowledge, our project plays a pivotal role. The earlier a disease is diagnosed, the better the chances of successful treatment. Our AI-driven model serves as a valuable tool, offering individuals a preliminary understanding of whether they may have pneumonia or not. More than a thousand x-rays have been evaluated in the web interface, offering insightful input and confirming its dependability and usability. This exemplifies the potential of AI to address real-world challenges, effectively merging cutting-edge AI technology with the practical realities of the medical field. In essence, our project represents one of the promising approaches to addressing issues related to medical diagnosis.

articleTitle: Deciphering the Unreplicable: Machine Learning Paradigms for Assessing and Manipulating Physical Unclonable Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Physically unclonable functions, such as inscription key generators, take advantage of their inherent physical distinctions. Even with promises of immunity to modelling and challenge- response pair prediction, the introduction of machine learning techniques presents a problem. Machine learning is a great tool for data extraction and system modelling because of its analytical strength and adaptability, especially when it comes to preventing attacks on systems that are physically difficult to recreate. This work extends earlier approaches by first creating a 64-bit binary dataset with Field Programmable Gate Array design tools, then modifying the dataset labels and optimising performance measures. The study employs four machine learning strategies, each with a distinct accuracy rate. K-fold logistic regression attains an accuracy of 50.11 percent, which is marginally more than support vector machines' precision of 49.50 percent. By comparison, a random forest classifier employing K-fold yields an accuracy rate of 49.00 percent; however, deep learning performs exceptionally well, with an astounding precision rate of 82.01 percent. This study attempts to evaluate PUF susceptibility by presenting accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity values.

articleTitle: Integration of Voice Assistant with ChatGPT and DALL-E
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: This paper discusses the integration of voice assistant with ChatGPT and Dall-E. JANY is an app that allows users to interact with the app using voice and it gets the subsequent response in speech as well as in text format. In the present-day context, the significance of voice interactions cannot be overstated, as they play a vital role in providing a seamless experience. Our approach involves converting speech to text, where the resulting text acts as an input for ChatGPT and DALL-E, followed by transforming the responses from text to speech. This is done taking into consideration people who can't read or write, the blind, old people, etc. The use of voice assistants integrated with AI like ChatGPT and DALL-E has tremendous potential as it provides an easy user experience and can also be accessed by people who have difficulty using traditional text-based interactions. Further, the paper also discusses the challenges encountered while integrating voice assistants with ChatGPT and DALL-E and how we overcame these challenges. The paper covers the system architecture, API calls, and libraries that were utilized, along with code snippets where required.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Scalable Federated Learning-Based Agricultural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Although agriculture is a substantial part of the Indian economy, it encounters several challenges. Precision agri-culture is a farming management strategy that aims to overcome these challenges. It optimizes several components of the farming process using data and technology, resulting in increased crop yields while reducing waste and raising total resource use effi-ciency. Thus, in its context, we present a study on the development of a Federated Learning-based Agricultural Network consisting of a popular federated learning algorithm FedAvg to perform image classification on an open dataset, Plant Village. In this work, we specifically analyze the performance of the proposed Federated Learning-based Agricultural Network in terms of its scalable deployment. The proposed network yields an average classification accuracy of 97.52 % on test data <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(C\approx 70)$</tex>, and provides a host of other benefits it derives from its federated nature, such as upholding the privacy of local client data as only the model updates are shared between the clients and the aggregation server. The prime objective of our work has been to study and explore the possibility of applying federated learning in the agriculture sector so that more efficient and privacy- preserving smart farming networks could be developed.

articleTitle: Neural Architecture Search Applied to Autoencoders Trained on Noisy Industrial Data: Single and Multi-Objective Investigations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has emerged as a powerful technique for automatically designing neural network architectures, offering the potential to discover models with superior performance and efficiency compared to manually designed architectures. In this study, we explore the application of NAS to autoencoder architectures, aiming to find models that provide the best trade-off between model complexity and reconstruction accuracy. Initially, we manually designed and evaluated several autoencoder architectures based on intuition, seeking to identify a baseline for comparison. Subsequently, we employed a Differential Evolution (DE) approach to perform NAS, searching for architectures that minimize the number of parameters, the number of nodes in the Latent Layer, and the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) simultaneously. Our results demonstrate that NAS can identify models with improved objective values compared to manually designed architectures. Furthermore, we developed a Non-dominated Sorting Differential Evolution (NSDE) approach tailored for multi-objective optimization in NAS. We applied NSDE to the same set of objectives and observed its ability to identify diverse and high-quality architectures.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Coherent & Non-Coherent MIMO Radar for Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Modern radar systems are essential for various applications, including defence, meteorology, and surveillance. Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar systems have gained significant attention due to their ability to improve target detection and tracking capabilities. Coherent and non-coherent MIMO radar systems differ in their signal processing approaches, with coherent systems offering better performance at the cost of increased computational complexity. This study focuses on the performance evaluation of coherent and non-coherent MIMO radar systems for target detection, aiming to improve the capacity and quality of efficiency in radar systems. This paper presents a comprehensive performance evaluation of coherent and non-coherent Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) radar systems for target detection. The study focuses on key parameters including Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR), Probability of False Detection, and Probability of Arrival. Coherent and non-coherent MIMO radar systems offer distinct advantages and trade-offs, making it essential to assess their performance under various conditions. Through simulation and analysis, this research aims to provide valuable insights into the comparative effectiveness of these radar architectures in detecting targets amidst noise and interference. Such insights can inform the design and implementation of radar systems tailored to specific operational requirements and environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Motor-Imagery Signal Preprocessing Using the SMOTE Technique and Neuromuscular Disorder Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Decoding motor imagery (MI) signals with precision is essential for brain-computer interface (BCI) systems utilized in healthcare applications. The majority of electroencephalographic (EEG) signals are time-domain recordings with distinct frequency components linked to particular brain activity. The time-domain data for EEG signals is a depiction of the electrical voltage variations across time. In this work, we looked at how combining classifiers based on wavelet features can help BCI systems classify EEG signals more accurately. Ten healthy individuals were told to see the right hand moving at predetermined intervals and perform “open” and “close” operations during data acquisition. Three electrodes have been placed on the individuals' scalps to collect data. Imbalanced MI-EEG data has proved difficult in recent years. Eliminating imbalanced MI-EEG channel data is the primary way to improve the performance of the classifying algorithms. Using machine learning techniques and MI-BCI-EEG channel imbalanced data processed with SMOTE will make it easier to look through huge amounts of data to find lies. This system used SMOTE to eliminate the unbalanced EEG channel data set. To enhance system performance and facilitate lie detection, these balanced data sets are trained with multiple classifiers, including KNN, DT, LR, RF, and SVM. This algorithm compares performance parameters such as accuracy, F1 score, specificity, precision, and sensitivity. Based on the results of the experiment, the SVM method attains the most remarkable accuracy of 98.3% when applied to the MI-BCI-EEG dataset.

articleTitle: Nuchal Translucency Assessment in Prenatal Screening: An Attention-Based U-Net Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Accurate identification and measurement of nuchal translucency (NT) region from fetal ultrasound images is critical in prenatal screening for chromosomal and congenital disorders. However, manual demarcation of the NT region can be difficult and subject to inter-operator heterogeneity. This work describes an automated solution for nuchal translucency segmentation based on an Attention U-Net architecture. The suggested method builds on the U -Net model's strengths for biomedical image segmentation by incorporating an attention mechanism that improves the model's capacity to focus on relevant characteristics and capture long-range dependencies. The Attention U-Net model is trained on a large dataset of fetal ultrasound images, and its performance can be evaluated using a different metrics, including Dice Similarity Coefficient, Jaccard Index, Specificity, Sensitivity and Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC-ROC) as 0.91, 0.8, 96.17, 96.17 and 99.8 respectively. The findings indicate that the suggested method outperforms standard U-Net and traditional image processing techniques, with high segmentation accuracy as 99.7 and robust performance across a variety of imaging conditions.

articleTitle: Vision Based Lane Assistance System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Autonomous navigation systems for robots are becoming increasingly essential in various domains, including transportation, surveillance, and logistics. Addressing the challenge of lane keeping is fundamental for safe and efficient navigation, mirroring the capabilities of human drivers. In this work, we present a camera-sensor based deep learning lane keeping system to autonomously move robots while guaranteeing they stay in defined lanes. The need for such a system arises from the rising demand for autonomous robotic solutions in real-world scenarios, where precise lane adherence is critical for safety and effectiveness. By leveraging convolutional neural networks (CNNs), our system accurately detects lane boundaries in real-time, ensuring robustness across diverse environmental conditions. A closed-loop control mechanism translates the CNN output into steering commands, facilitating smooth and precise navigation. Through extensive simulations and real-world experiments, we demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of our approach, contributing to the advancement of autonomous robotic systems and enhancing their capability for safe and reliable navigation in various applications.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Analytical Framework for Predicting Fuel Consumption in Shipping Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as revolutionary fields with immense potential as technology continues to influence our world. Automation has been transformed by AI and ML, increasing productivity and efficiency for enterprises. Automation increases productivity and reduces operating costs by streamlining operations, which makes it a desirable option for businesses looking to maintain their competitiveness. The need for experts in AI and ML is growing as a result of these fields' exponential growth. A growing number of business operations in the shipping sector, including fleet management, predictive maintenance, autonomous shipping, cargo optimisation, risk management, and supply chain infrastructure, are being made simpler, better, and more scalable through the application of AI and ML. As the shipping industry uses AI and ML to process and analyse massive volumes of data, improve decision-making, offer recommendations and insights in real time, and produce precise forecasts and predictions, these solutions are becoming more and more common. Although sales, marketing, and finance in the shipping industry can also benefit from AI/ML, traditional methods of shipment confront issues with accuracy, adaptability, and inefficiency. Thus, we proposed an AI/ML-based solution for increasing efficiency and adaptability in the shipment process for various companies and industries. We have employed machine learning (ML) algorithms to reduce inefficiencies and costs in the shipment process. Our proposed framework uses a linear regression model with a minimum error rate (0.001) compared to other ML algorithms. Further, we have used neural networks for classification between efficiencies of the ship, i.e. we have classified the ship as a ship with good or bad efficiency with deep learning (DL) models and produced an accuracy of 94.38%.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Black Fungus Using Deep Learning Models for Efficient Medical Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Mucormycosis, also known as black fungus, is a rare infection caused by mould that can affect the lungs, brain, skin, and sinuses. People with weakened immune systems due to underlying health conditions (e.g., organ transplant, uncontrolled diabetes, cancer, neutropenia, AIDS, and COVID-19) or drug use are more likely to contract the infection. Recent reports have indicated that a small number of COVID-19 survivors with co-morbidities are particularly vulnerable to black fungus. Therefore, recovered COVID-19 patients should seek medical attention immediately if they experience any mucormycosis symptoms. Patients with COVID-19 have numerous concerns regarding this life-threatening infection, particularly those with immunocompromised states such as solid organ transplant (SOT) and hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) or tumors, who are more likely to be infected. Early diagnosis and treatment are essential to prevent patient mortality. In this paper, we present the Multi-Class Black Fungus (MCBF) dataset, which consists of three compressed folders containing images. The first folder includes 66 images of eye black fungus after data preprocessing, while the second folder contains 63 images of mouth black fungus after data preprocessing. The third contains 62 images of the mouth after applying data preprocessing, and the last one contains 79 images of black skin fungus after applying data preprocessing. The MCBF dataset contains images that aid in training and validation when using deep learning algorithms to recognise and classify black fungus diseases, then we apply a resnet(50) pretrained model by using MCBF accuracy reaches 96.12%.

articleTitle: AstroFusion: A GAN-Augmented Approach for Exoplanet Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Humanity's exploration of the cosmos spans billions of years, prompting contemplation of our position in the universe. This study advocates for proactive communication with potential intelligent species, driven by uncertainty about their existence. The focus is on exploring Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to enhance exoplanet detection through data augmentation. Utilizing the extensive Kepler dataset, the study evaluates the accuracy of conventional machine learning techniques: Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, and Random Forests. (RF)-trained on original data. Subsequently, it assesses the effectiveness of models trained solely on GAN-generated synthetic data and compares their performance with that of models trained on original data. Lastly, it merges original and synthetic data to create a composite dataset, evaluating the ML model's accuracy. The results indicate that models trained solely on synthetic data achieve comparable accuracy to those trained on original data. Furthermore, the combined dataset yields improved accuracy-87%, 95%, and 96% in Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and RF, respectively-highlighting the potential of GAN-based data augmentation in enhancing exoplanet detection. This study advances space exploration by integrating technology with astronomical research, facilitating more precise and reliable exoplanet detection methods. Leveraging GANs for data augmentation promises novel insights and discoveries about the universe.

articleTitle: A Novel Direct Formula Based Technique for Predicting the Class Label of New Unseen Test Tuple without Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: Supervised learning is an important task in many machine learning applications. In this paper, a direct formula is proposed for predicting the class label of a generalized new unseen instance. The mostimportant attractive feature of the proposed class label prediction formula is that it requires no training step. In other words, intermediate learning steps are not required and as a result of this there exists no intermediate models for class label prediction. Proposed formula directly predicts class label of thenew test tuple. Proposed class label prediction formula is based on the aggregate class label counts of the values of the attributes of the given entire training dataset. For optimal performance, proposed formula is normalized and normalized formula is used for prediction. For brevity, proposed class label prediction technique is named as Direct Class Label Prediction (DCLP). Experiments are conducted on many of the UCI machine learning datasets.
